blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Mapping the flow of a supply chain means drawing, on paper or on screen, the exact path the product takes — from raw material to the customer's hand. Every step is shown. Every hand-off is shown. Every waiting moment, between one step and the next, is shown too.

The map is revealing. Most teams discover that they are waiting much more than they are working. An order sits in a queue. A pallet waits for a truck. A container waits for customs. A shipment waits for a signature. Actual productive time is often less than a quarter of the total.

Once the map is on the wall, improvements become obvious. You cannot fix delays you cannot see, and you cannot see delays you have not mapped. Mapping is step zero — and almost always worth the hour.

items.q: According to the text, what does mapping a supply chain involve drawing?
options: The cost of each step in the process
The exact path the product takes, from raw material to the customer
Only the steps that add value
The organisation chart of the supply team
items.why: "drawing… the exact path the product takes — from raw material to the customer's hand."

items.q: What do most teams discover once the map is complete?
options: That customs is always to blame
That they are waiting much more than they are working
That their trucks are too slow
That they have too many suppliers
items.why: "Most teams discover that they are waiting much more than they are working."

items.q: The text says actual productive time is often…
options: less than a quarter of the total
more than half of the total
items.why: "Actual productive time is often less than a quarter of the total."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely AGREE with?
options: Productive time is usually the biggest part of the journey
A map is only useful for large factories
Delays should be fixed before they are mapped
The waiting between steps matters as much as the steps themselves
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que cada momento de espera é mostrado — o tempo entre etapas é o principal achado.

items.q: What does "Mapping is step zero" suggest about the activity?
options: It comes before any attempt to improve the process
It should be done last, after improvements
It has no real value on its own
It is the least important step
items.why: Inferência: "step zero" indica que o mapeamento precede tudo — sem ver o atraso, não dá para corrigi-lo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily conduzindo a oficina de mapeamento com a equipe da fábrica. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, everyone — before we improve anything, we're going to draw it. One shipment. One journey. From the raw material arriving at the gate to the box landing on the customer's desk. Nothing is skipped.

So let's start. The raw material is received here. It's inspected, then it's moved to the line. Notice I'm saying "is received", "is inspected" — the passive — because right now I care about what happens, not who does it. Keep the sticky notes coming.

Here's the part I want you to watch. Between these two steps, the pallet just sits. It's waiting for a truck. And here — the container is held at customs for two days. And here again — the whole shipment waits for one signature.

Look at the wall. The green notes are work; the red notes are waiting. There is far more red than green, and that always surprises people. We're not slow because the work is slow. We're slow because of the gaps between the work.

None of this was invented today. It was all there yesterday. The only difference is that now we can see it — and once you can see a delay, you can finally do something about it.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Emily insist the team do BEFORE improving anything?
options: Hire more staff for the line
Draw the whole journey of one shipment
items.why: "before we improve anything, we're going to draw it. One shipment. One journey."

items.q: Why does Emily use the passive ("is received", "is inspected")?
options: Because the factory rules require it
Because she does not know who does the work
Because it sounds more polite to the team
Because she cares about what happens, not who does it
items.why: "the passive — because right now I care about what happens, not who does it."

items.q: What do the red sticky notes on the wall represent?
items.why: "The green notes are work; the red notes are waiting."

items.q: What does Emily mean by "We're slow because of the gaps between the work"?
options: The waiting between steps, not the work itself, causes the delay
The machines break down too often
The workers are not skilled enough
There are not enough steps in the process
items.why: Inferência: ela contrasta trabalho (verde) com espera (vermelho) — o gargalo está nas lacunas, não na execução.

items.q: What is Emily's main point in the final part of the talk?
options: The delays already existed; mapping simply makes them visible
The map creates the delays it shows
Customs is the only cause of the delays
The delays are new problems created today
items.why: Inferência: "None of this was invented today… now we can see it" — o mapa revela, não cria, os atrasos.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Each hand-off between shifts is where information gets lost." A hand-off is…
options: the point where responsibility passes from one party to the next
items.why: Hand-off = passagem: o ponto em que uma etapa entrega o trabalho à seguinte.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The order sat in a ___ for three days before anyone picked it up."
items.why: Queue = fila; o pedido ficou esperando na fila antes de ser processado.

items.q: "Only a quarter of the cycle is genuinely productive." Productive time is time that…
options: actually adds value to the product
items.why: Productive = produtivo: o tempo que de fato agrega valor, em oposição à espera.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The whole shipment was stuck because one ___ was missing from the release form."
items.why: Signature = assinatura; faltava a assinatura para liberar a carga.

items.q: "Once you draw the flow, the bottleneck is easy to spot." The flow is…
options: the path the work follows through the process
the number of workers on the line
the total cost of the shipment
items.why: Flow = fluxo: o caminho que o trabalho percorre de ponta a ponta.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre processos e operações. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's map out the whole journey before we change a single step." To map out means to…
options: hand a task to someone else
plan or lay out something in detail
items.why: Map out = traçar/planejar em detalhe cada parte de algo.

items.q: "We need to iron out the delays at customs." To iron out means to…
items.why: Iron out = resolver, eliminar as arestas de um problema.

items.q: "The pallet is just sitting idle while it waits for a truck." Sitting idle means…
items.why: Sitting idle = parado, sem uso — nenhum trabalho está sendo feito.

items.q: "Fixing that one hand-off could really speed up the whole line." To speed up means to…
items.why: Speed up = acelerar, tornar mais rápido.

items.q: "Cutting one signature won't move the needle on our lead time." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
